brad-jacobs.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
brad-jacobs.summary: No reviewed source documents a wealth–political-power mechanism for Jacobs. Searches for political donations, government ties and conflicts connected to XPO and QXO returned only business coverage, and one further search was not possible. This is a narrow review, not exoneration.
brad-jacobs.mechanism: None documented in the sources reviewed

support.text: The reviewed profile establishes Jacobs as the founder and executive behind XPO, its GXO and RXO spin-offs and QXO. This is a role and business-history fact; it does not establish any political mechanism.
support.kind: Role and identity only; not evidence of a mechanism
support.access: Page text reviewed; secondary tertiary-source summary, not a primary record

counter.text: The reviewed Wikipedia profile lists his XPO spin-offs, GXO and RXO, and QXO’s acquisitions, including Beacon in April 2025, as business transactions. It contains no information on political donations, government ties or legal or regulatory controversies. Absence on one summary page does not prove none exists.
counter.access: Page text reviewed; secondary tertiary-source summary, not a primary record

brad-jacobs.limitations: Not a comprehensive search of FEC, lobbying, SEC or court records. A New York Times analysis of post-election donors surfaced in a search but could not be opened (HTTP 403), so no claim is made about whether he appears in it. Wealth, company size and acquisitions alone give no points.

jan-koum.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
jan-koum.summary: Koum is reported as a large Republican and pro-Israel political donor. The reviewed sources document giving, not a policy outcome, preferential benefit or feedback loop, so no estimate is made.
jan-koum.mechanism: Large political donations; no linked benefit documented

support.text: Mission Local reports a $250,000 gift on 13 April 2026 to San Francisco’s S.F. Believes PAC, which backs measures and allies of Mayor Daniel Lurie. It also reports he gave a little over $5 million to MAGA Inc. in 2024 and $1 million in 2025, and $500,000 to an earlier pro-Lurie PAC in 2024.

counter.text: The same article says Lurie does not control the PAC, whose treasurers declined to comment, and reports no stated purpose or response from Koum. It identifies no benefit he obtained.
counter.source: Mission Local: limits of the evidence

counter.text: JTA’s 2022 profile of his philanthropy says no one would speak on the record about his motivations and that his foundation did not comment. Its donation figures concern charities, not government contracts or policy.
counter.kind: Subject response absent; limit of evidence

jan-koum.limitations: Donations alone do not justify points. Koum left Facebook in 2018 and no current regulatory or contract stake was identified. Search snippets about AIPAC and Haley gifts came from secondary pages that were not opened and are not relied on. This is a narrow review, not an exoneration.

zhou-qunfei.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
zhou-qunfei.summary: Lens Technology recognized government subsidies and has regular official engagement, and Zhou attended a May 2026 state banquet. zhou-qunfei.mechanism: Company subsidies and official contact; personal mechanism not shown

RMB 347 million came from the Liuyang Economic Development Zone, equal to 14.17% of the latest audited net profit. It also reports a provincial vice governor visiting in August 2024.

support.text: The Wikipedia profile, citing the South China Morning Post of 15 May 2026, says she was seated between Tim Cook and Elon Musk at the state banquet Xi Jinping hosted for Donald Trump.
support.access: Page text reviewed; secondary tertiary-source summary, not a primary record

counter.text: The Wikipedia profile mentions no NPC or CPPCC role, party office, subsidy or controversy and does not say the banquet seat reflects a formal government relationship. It carries a promotional-content tag.
counter.access: Page text reviewed; secondary tertiary-source summary, not a primary record

counter.text: The NL Times article does not name Zhou. Local subsidies and provincial visits are common in Chinese industrial policy and do not show a personal bargain; it describes standards drafting and collaboration with CAS-incubated firms.

zhou-qunfei.limitations: Not a review of her political positions: official NPC/CPPCC lists and Lens filings were not checked, and further searches were not possible. A Vietnamese-language search result and Apple revenue share claims were not opened. Family members were not individually assessed. This is a narrow review, not an exoneration.

lu-xiangyang.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
lu-xiangyang.summary: Lu is identified as a BYD co-founder and early investor. The reviewed page lists no political role or documented state exchange attributable to him personally, and BYD-wide state support was not researched here. This is not exoneration.

support.text: The reviewed profile identifies Lu as an early BYD investor and co-founder alongside his cousin Wang Chuanfu. This is a role and identity fact; it does not establish any political mechanism.

support.access: Page text reviewed; secondary tertiary-source summary, not a primary record

counter.kind: Identity and explicit limit of the evidence
counter.access: Page text reviewed; secondary tertiary-source summary, not a primary record

lu-xiangyang.limitations: Identity: a search indicated Forbes’ Lu Xiangyang is the BYD co-founder (also written Lv Xiangyang); not independently verified against Forbes. arthur-dantchik.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
arthur-dantchik.summary: Dantchik, with Susquehanna co-principals, was reported to have funded school-choice political efforts and Susquehanna companies received state education tax credits. The reviewed sources do not show that the giving obtained those credits or any other preferential outcome; the donors dispute the benefit claim.
arthur-dantchik.mechanism: School-choice political funding alongside state tax-credit use; causation unproven

support.text: WHYY reports Susquehanna principals Jeff Yass, Joel Greenberg and Dantchik gave more than $5 million, much through the Students First PAC, to Anthony Williams’s 2010 governor campaign and funded a 2015 mayoral ad effort. The article does not break out Dantchik’s share. A rival campaign said they benefited from about $5 million in tax credits; WHYY reported Susquehanna-associated companies received over $4.3 million in credits in the previous year.
support.kind: Reported donations and tax-credit use; opponent claim

support.text: Haaretz, as summarized on Wikipedia, reports Dantchik’s CLAWS Foundation gave more than $25 million to the Shalom Hartman Institute in 2010–2020 and funded Kohelet; Kohelet is described as influential in the 2023 Israeli judicial overhaul. Ynet quotes him saying he stopped donating to Israeli think tanks, including Kohelet, to promote national unity.
support.access: Page text reviewed; secondary tertiary-source summary, not a primary record

counter.text: The same WHYY article quotes Greenberg calling the donations “purely altruistic,” and says the donors did not profit because the credits do not fully reimburse contributions. It reports no comment from Dantchik.
Ynet attributes the Kohelet judicial-overhaul characterization to the article itself, not an independent finding, and records his withdrawal of funding in 2023.
counter.kind: Limit of evidence and subject statement

arthur-dantchik.limitations: Dated and mostly about the group, not him alone. Education tax-credit programs are statutory and open to qualifying donors. Wikipedia’s claim about his ByteDance board role was not relied on. No current Susquehanna regulatory or lobbying matter was documented; a search for prediction-market lobbying found nothing. Not exoneration.

george-kaiser.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
george-kaiser.period: Solyndra loan guarantee 2009; White House contacts 2009–2010; bankruptcy 2011; IG report 2015
george-kaiser.summary: Kaiser was a major Obama donor and White House visitor, and in 2010 his associates pressed officials for a second Solyndra loan that was not approved. The reviewed records support access and a possible influence channel, not a documented favor to him; the DOE Inspector General attributed the 2009 loan problems chiefly to Solyndra’s misstatements.
george-kaiser.mechanism: Donor access and lobbying for a portfolio company; favor not established

support.text: AP, via NBC News, reports Kaiser was a frequent White House visitor in 2009–2010 and pushed officials in 2010 for a second Solyndra loan, which was not approved. Instead a Kaiser-controlled venture made a private loan that put it and other investors ahead of taxpayers if Solyndra defaulted. Solyndra, which received a $528 million loan in 2009, went bankrupt in September 2011.

The same article says White House officials denied for months that Kaiser discussed Solyndra on his visits, and a released March 2010 email from his associate Steve Mitchell said Energy Secretary Chu was “talking up the company.” Rep. Cliff Stearns said Kaiser’s employees “exercised influence throughout the loan process.”
support.source: AP / NBC News: emails and committee claim

counter.text: White House spokesman Eric Schultz said the loan was “a decision made on the merits” and the documents show no “favoritism to political supporters.” The article reports no official finding of improper influence.
counter.source: AP / NBC News: White House response

counter.text: The DOE Inspector General report of 24 August 2015 found Solyndra’s statements to DOE inaccurate and misleading and DOE’s review ineffective. It did not make political pressure its focus, although staff described pressure to process applications. The article does not mention Kaiser.
counter.source: Power Magazine on DOE OIG report, 27 Aug 2015
counter.kind: Official finding on cause; limit of the evidence

george-kaiser.limitations: Historical single episode, not a current assessment. The loan went to Solyndra, not personally to Kaiser, and the company failed, so a personal preferential gain is not shown; his priority position came from a private loan. Other Kaiser interests (banking, oil and gas) and Oklahoma politics were not reviewed. The Public Integrity article on his fundraising returned an error and is not cited.
